request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "My crew due" figure (`my-crew-due-total`). It's the due-totals of every crew led by the signed-in user's person, added up. When that person leads no crew, or no person matches the user, it's blank. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

It finds "the user's person" the same way the existing "My due" figure does: a person whose name or alias matches the signed-in name, ignoring case. That's why the test passes once Cam is given the alias "Uma": the user uma then counts as leading Cam's crew.

This was a front-end change only, because crews and their due-totals were already worked out in the browser:
- **`features/crews/crews.ts`**: I moved the crew due-total sum into a shared function, `crewDueTotal()`. The crews list is now kept in the `CrewRoster` service, so other parts of the screen can read it.
- **`features/people/people.ts`**: it now works out the crew total from that list and the people's due-totals, and passes it to the header. I also split out the user-to-person matching so "My due" and the crew total share it.
- **`features/header/header.ts`**: it has the new input and the new figure.

Nothing changed on the server, in the stored data, or in the audit file; the test expects no new audit records.
